fact_sheet.story_hook: Victims who have already lost money to scams are targeted by fraudsters posing as 'anti-scam firms' or legal experts. These scammers promise to help recover lost funds with unusually high success rates, often demanding upfront fees or personal banking details, only to defraud the victim of even more money.
fact_sheet.red_flag: Be immediately suspicious of any individual or organisation that guarantees or promises unusually high success rates for recovering lost scam funds, especially if they request upfront payments, processing fees, or sensitive personal and banking information.
fact_sheet.the_fix: If you suspect you have fallen victim to a fraudulent recovery service, immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) hotline at 997. Also, report the incident to your bank and file a police report at the nearest police station as soon as possible. Remember, official bodies like PDRM and NSRC do not use private channels or request payments for investigations or fund recovery.

obfuscated_story.title: The Double Blow: Beware of Fraudulent Fund Recovery Scams
obfuscated_story.summary: Victims who have already lost money to initial scams are being targeted a second time by fraudsters posing as legal recovery experts. These scammers promise to retrieve lost funds in exchange for upfront fees and personal data, only to disappear with more of the victim's money.
obfuscated_story.story: After losing RM50,000 in a fraudulent investment scheme, a victim is contacted on social media by an individual claiming to be a 'Senior Recovery Consultant' from a prestigious-sounding legal firm. The consultant claims they have special access to the banking backend and can track the stolen funds through international servers. They guarantee a 95% success rate, preying on the victim's desperation to recover their savings. The scammer sends a series of forged legal documents and fake testimonials from other 'successful' clients to build trust. Once the victim is hooked, the consultant demands an 'administrative processing fee' of RM3,000 to initiate the recovery process. Thinking this is their only chance, the victim pays the fee. Shortly after, the scammer requests the victim's online banking credentials, claiming they need to 'verify' the incoming recovered funds. Using this information, the scammer clears out the victim's remaining balance. The victim realizes too late that they have been scammed twice when the consultant's profile vanishes and the phone number goes dead.
obfuscated_story.solution: If you suspect you have fallen victim to a fraudulent recovery service, immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997. Additionally, report the incident to your bank's fraud hotline and file an official report at the nearest PDRM station. Do not share your banking credentials or pay upfront fees to private entities claiming to recover funds.
red_flags: Guarantees or promises of unusually high success rates for recovering lost scam funds
Requests for upfront payments, legal fees, or administrative charges to start a recovery process
Demands for sensitive personal data or online banking login credentials
Communications through private messaging apps or unofficial social media profiles claiming to represent official bodies
